strips.hook: [device: attendance-amnesia] [target: AI at work | form: three-hander (rotating pair) | aim: inward | mechanic: illusion demolition | cast: Susie + Cal + Milo] Three people were all on the same 41-minute call. The only one who knows what got agreed is reading it off the AI recap. Radar seed: Lobsters 'Prevent cognitive debt by manually retyping LLM-generated code' + Techmeme 'Apple caps AI-assisted bug reports' + SaaStr/20VC 'The Agent That Rewrote My Code Without Telling Me' — the cluster of outsourcing comprehension to a machine.
strips.caption:
You were on the call. You still read the recap.

Forty-one minutes, camera on, fully present — and the only reason you know what you agreed to is a summary a machine wrote. Attendance and memory quietly stopped being the same thing.

strips.hook: [device: euphemism-unmasked] [target: corporate euphemism | form: two-hander | aim: systemic | mechanic: etymological-unmasking (#14) | cast: Cal + Milo (Milo debut)] A new SDR asks why his prospect's VP is suddenly CC'd on his follow-up. Cal says 'for visibility' — and it turns out to be literally accurate: the VP can't help, only watch. Cal's rule for the move (one per deal, spent when the deal is already dead) reveals he wrote Milo's deal off this morning. Radar seed: scout Source 1 (SaaStr AI SDRs — 3,221 emails/mo vs 75-285, reply rates flat) + Techmeme (Apple caps bug-report submissions over an AI-assisted deluge) => volume never applies pressure; the CC to someone's boss is how humans actually do it. News-deleted, the strip is unchanged.
strips.caption:
"Adding Priya for visibility."

Everyone in B2B knows exactly what that sentence means. Nobody has ever written down what it means.

strips.hook: [device: ritual-as-agency] [target: the protagonists' own failings | form: two-hander | aim: inward | mechanic: anti-work-equilibrium | cast: Milo+Cal] You refresh the inbox that would have pinged you anyway - not for the reply, for the one thing at work that responds the second you ask. (2-panel recut: the 3-panel original was killed under S13, user 2026-08-02 - the reveal closed in panel 2 and panel 3 topped it.)
strips.caption: The button is the only one that answers.

strips.hook: [device: process-recursion] [target: bureaucratic process | form: two-hander | aim: systemic | mechanic: policy-as-punchline | cast: Milo+Frank] The cheap purchase is the slow one — the fix is to spend more. Standalone; references nothing outside its own three panels. Scored 29/30 by independent craft judges in two separate rounds and passed the cold-scroller gate in both.
